keyPoints: Light DOM children stay in the main document tree and project visually into matching <slot>s.
Content inside <slot>Fallback</slot> displays only when no matching node is assigned.
Listen to the slotchange event to react when projected children are added or removed.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to select slotted descendants with .card h3 inside Shadow CSS
commonMistakes.fix: Shadow CSS cannot descend into slotted trees; use ::slotted(h3) for top-level slotted elements.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting that slot="..." only works on direct children of the custom element host
commonMistakes.fix: Place the slot attribute directly on a top-level child of the custom element.

interviewQA.question: Where do slotted elements physically live in the DOM?
interviewQA.answer: They remain in the host’s light DOM and are merely projected visually into the Shadow DOM’s composed tree.

interviewQA.question: When does fallback content inside <slot> appear?
interviewQA.answer: Whenever zero light-DOM nodes are assigned to that slot.

lessons.title: Form-Associated Custom Elements (ElementInternals)
lessons.summary: Standard custom elements do not participate in <form> submission until they opt in via static formAssociated = true and attachInternals().
explanation: Standard custom elements do not participate in <form> submission until they opt in via static formAssociated = true and attachInternals().
ElementInternals lets a custom control register its value with FormData, report Constraint Validation errors via setValidity(), and respond to formResetCallback().
Use ElementInternals when building design-system inputs like custom date pickers or tag inputs that must work inside plain HTML forms.

codeExample.title: Using a Form-Associated Custom Control
codeExample.code:
<form action="/profile" method="post">
  <label for="rating">Confidence Score</label>
  <star-rating id="rating" name="confidence" value="4"></star-rating>
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>

keyPoints: static formAssociated = true enables native <form> integration for custom elements.
internals.setFormValue(val) includes the custom element in FormData automatically.
internals.setValidity() connects custom components to native browser validation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting <my-input name="x"> to appear in FormData automatically
commonMistakes.fix: Unless static formAssociated = true and setFormValue() are implemented, forms ignore custom elements.

commonMistakes.mistake: Skipping formResetCallback()
commonMistakes.fix: Implement formResetCallback() so clicking <button type="reset"> restores the custom control’s default value.

interviewQA.question: What API lets a Web Component integrate with native <form> validation and FormData?
interviewQA.answer: ElementInternals via this.attachInternals() combined with static formAssociated = true.

interviewQA.question: Can ElementInternals also set default ARIA roles on a custom element?
interviewQA.answer: Yes—internals.role and internals.ariaChecked set default accessibility states without cluttering host HTML attributes.

sections.title: Performance, Security & Browser Pipeline
sections.description: Optimize Critical Rendering Path, resource priority hints, CSP hardening, and Subresource Integrity.

lessons.title: Critical Rendering Path, Preload & fetchpriority
lessons.summary: HTML markup directly controls how quickly the browser discovers, fetches, and paints the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element.
explanation: HTML markup directly controls how quickly the browser discovers, fetches, and paints the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element.
The browser’s HTML preload scanner scans raw markup for , , and
Avoid overusing rel="preload"—preloading too many assets starves the actual LCP resource of bandwidth.

codeExample.title: Optimizing LCP Discovery & Font Preloading

keyPoints: Font preloads MUST include the crossorigin attribute or the browser downloads the font twice.
fetchpriority="high" elevates the hero image ahead of lower-priority scripts.
Keep critical hero images directly in HTML rather than hidden behind CSS background-image.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting crossorigin on <link rel="preload" as="font">
commonMistakes.fix: Fonts are always fetched in CORS mode; omitting crossorigin causes a double download.

commonMistakes.mistake: Preloading 10+ assets in <head>
commonMistakes.fix: Preload only the 1–2 truly critical LCP resources so bandwidth stays focused.

interviewQA.question: Why must <link rel="preload" as="font"> include the crossorigin attribute even for same-origin fonts?
interviewQA.answer: The CSS Fonts specification requires fonts to be fetched with CORS credentials mode anonymous; without crossorigin, the preload cache key mismatches the CSS request and downloads twice.

interviewQA.question: Why is faster for LCP than a CSS background-image?
interviewQA.answer: The HTML preload scanner discovers immediately in the initial HTML stream, whereas CSS background images cannot be discovered until CSS is downloaded, parsed, and matched to DOM nodes.

lessons.title: Subresource Integrity (SRI) & Cross-Origin Policies
lessons.summary: When loading scripts or stylesheets from third-party CDNs, Subresource Integrity verifies a cryptographic hash before execution.
explanation: When loading scripts or stylesheets from third-party CDNs, Subresource Integrity verifies a cryptographic hash before execution.
If a CDN is compromised and the file bytes change by even one character, the browser refuses to execute the script because its SHA-384 digest no longer matches the integrity attribute.
Always pair integrity with crossorigin="anonymous" so the browser can read the response bytes and verify the hash.

codeExample.title: Subresource Integrity on External Assets
codeExample.code:
<script
  src="https://cdn.example.net/lib@2.1.0/index.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC"
  crossorigin="anonymous"
  defer
></script>

keyPoints: SRI protects against compromised third-party CDNs using SHA-256/384/512 hashes.
crossorigin="anonymous" is required for SRI checks on cross-origin URLs.
Pin exact version URLs—never use SRI on mutable /latest/ URLs that change silently.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding integrity to a mutable CDN URL like /library@latest.js
commonMistakes.fix: When the CDN updates @latest, the hash mismatches and breaks your production site; always pin immutable version URLs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Omitting crossorigin="anonymous" alongside integrity
commonMistakes.fix: Without CORS headers and crossorigin, browsers cannot inspect cross-origin bytes to validate SRI.

interviewQA.question: What happens if an external script fails its Subresource Integrity check?
interviewQA.answer: The browser blocks execution completely and logs a security error to the console, protecting users from supply-chain tampering.

interviewQA.question: Which hash algorithms are valid in the integrity attribute?
interviewQA.answer: sha256, sha384, and sha512 (base64-encoded); sha384 is the common default.

lessons.title: HTML Security: XSS Prevention & Content Security Policy
lessons.summary: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when untrusted strings are injected into HTML markup or event attributes without proper escaping.
explanation: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when untrusted strings are injected into HTML markup or event attributes without proper escaping.

Never concatenate untrusted input into innerHTML or inline attributes like onclick="..." or href="javascript:...". Combine context-aware escaping with a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) disallowing inline scripts.
Use textContent instead of innerHTML whenever inserting plain text into the DOM.

codeExample.title: Safe DOM Rendering vs CSP Meta Tag
codeExample.code: Verify

keyPoints: Escape HTML special characters or use textContent when rendering user strings.
Validate URL schemes (allow only https:, http:, mailto:) to block javascript: XSS.
A strict CSP without unsafe-inline blocks injected inline script execution.

commonMistakes.mistake: Allowing arbitrary user URLs directly into <a href={userUrl}>
commonMistakes.fix: Check new URL(userUrl).protocol is http: or https: so javascript:alert(1) cannot execute on click.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using innerHTML to display a user’s display name
commonMistakes.fix: Use textContent (or React JSX text interpolation) which never parses HTML tags.

interviewQA.question: Why isn’t HTML-escaping alone enough for <a href="USER_INPUT">?
interviewQA.answer: Even with < and > escaped, a value like javascript:fetch(...) is valid inside href and executes when clicked; you must validate the URL protocol.

interviewQA.question: How does Content-Security-Policy mitigate XSS?
interviewQA.answer: By restricting which origins and nonces are allowed to execute scripts, blocking attacker-injected inline <script> blocks even if an injection bug exists.

lessons.title: Speculation Rules & View Transitions Meta
lessons.summary: Modern HTML enables instant multi-page navigations using declarative Speculation Rules prerendering and cross-document View Transitions.
explanation: Modern HTML enables instant multi-page navigations using declarative Speculation Rules prerendering and cross-document View Transitions.

A <script type="speculationrules"> JSON block tells Chromium-based browsers which high-probability links to prefetch or prerender on hover/moderate eagerness, while maintaining graceful fallback in other browsers.
Only prerender idempotent GET pages—never prerender logout, checkout, or state-mutating URLs.

codeExample.title: Declarative Speculation Rules for Instant Navigation
codeExample.code:
<script type="speculationrules">
{
  "prerender": [
    {
      "where": { "href_matches": "/courses/*" },
      "eagerness": "moderate"
    }
  ]
}
</script>

keyPoints: type="speculationrules" is safely ignored by browsers that do not support it (progressive enhancement).
eagerness: "moderate" waits for pointer hover (~200ms), balancing speed and bandwidth.
Exclude state-changing endpoints like /logout or /cart/remove from prerender rules.

commonMistakes.mistake: Prerendering every link on a page with eagerness: "immediate"
commonMistakes.fix: Use moderate or conservative eagerness to avoid wasting mobile data and server load.

commonMistakes.mistake: Including /signout in a wildcard prerender pattern
commonMistakes.fix: Explicitly exclude mutating URLs with not href_matches rules.

interviewQA.question: How does Speculation Rules prerendering differ from <link rel="prefetch">?
interviewQA.answer: prefetch only downloads the HTML document into cache, whereas prerender loads, parses, and renders the full page in an invisible background tab for near-0ms navigation.

interviewQA.question: What happens in browsers that do not support type="speculationrules"?
interviewQA.answer: They treat the unknown script type as an inert data block with zero errors, preserving standard link navigation.

sections.title: HTML5 Browser APIs & Declarative Streaming
sections.description: Connect semantic HTML directly to native browser capabilities: data-* attributes, File/Clipboard APIs, Declarative Shadow DOM, and streaming SSR.

lessons.title: Custom data-* Attributes & Dataset Contracts
lessons.summary: HTML5 data-* attributes provide a standards-compliant namespace for attaching structured metadata to DOM elements without polluting global IDs or CSS classes.
explanation: HTML5 data-* attributes provide a standards-compliant namespace for attaching structured metadata to DOM elements without polluting global IDs or CSS classes.

Browsers map hyphenated attributes like data-course-slug="html" automatically to camelCase properties on element.dataset (el.dataset.courseSlug), while CSS can read them via [data-state="open"] or attr().
Keep data-* values small, non-sensitive strings—never store secrets, PII, or megabytes of serialized JSON in HTML attributes.

codeExample.title: Declarative State Hooks with data-* Attributes
codeExample.code:
<button
  type="button"
  data-course-slug="html"
  data-lesson-index="48"
  data-state="ready"
>
  Complete Lesson
</button>

keyPoints: Every custom data attribute must start with data- followed by lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens.
JavaScript reads and writes them via element.dataset using camelCase property names.
Styling via [data-state="active"] decouples UI state cleanly from utility or BEM class names.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using uppercase letters in data-userId attributes in HTML
commonMistakes.fix: HTML attribute names are lowercased by the parser; write data-user-id so dataset.userId maps predictably.

commonMistakes.mistake: Embedding auth tokens or raw user PII inside data-* attributes
commonMistakes.fix: Anyone can inspect DOM attributes via DevTools or third-party scripts; keep sensitive data server-side or in HttpOnly cookies.

interviewQA.question: How does data-quiz-score="95" map onto element.dataset in JavaScript?
interviewQA.answer: Hyphens are stripped and converted to camelCase, producing element.dataset.quizScore === "95" (always a string).

interviewQA.question: Why is [data-state="open"] often preferred over toggling .is-open classes?
interviewQA.answer: Attribute selectors enforce mutually exclusive states (e.g., idle, loading, open, error) instead of accumulating conflicting boolean classes.

lessons.title: Native File Inputs, Accept Filters & Drag-and-Drop
lessons.summary: HTML <input type="file"> combined with accept, multiple, and capture attributes provides accessible file selection across desktop and mobile devices without custom plugins.
explanation: HTML <input type="file"> combined with accept, multiple, and capture attributes provides accessible file selection across desktop and mobile devices without custom plugins.
Setting accept=".pdf,image/png,image/jpeg" guides the OS file picker, while the native Drag-and-Drop attributes (draggable="true") work alongside keyboard-accessible button alternatives.
Always re-validate uploaded file types and magic bytes on the server; HTML accept is a UX convenience, never a security barrier.

codeExample.title: Accessible Multi-File Upload Input
codeExample.code:
<label for="project-files">Upload project screenshots (PNG/JPG)</label>
<input
  id="project-files"
  name="screenshots"
  type="file"
  accept="image/png,image/jpeg"
  multiple
/>

keyPoints: accept filters file pickers by MIME type or file extension.
multiple allows selecting more than one file in a single dialog.
Always pair visual drag-and-drop zones with a real keyboard-focusable <input type="file">.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying solely on accept="image/png" for upload security
commonMistakes.fix: Users can select "All Files" or spoof requests; always inspect MIME/bytes server-side.

commonMistakes.mistake: Building a drag-and-drop upload box with no clickable/focusable file input
commonMistakes.fix: Keyboard and screen reader users cannot drag files with a mouse; always expose a labeled file input.

interviewQA.question: Why must a drag-and-drop file uploader still include a standard <input type="file">?
interviewQA.answer: To satisfy keyboard accessibility (WCAG 2.1.1) and support touch devices where desktop drag-and-drop does not exist.

interviewQA.question: What does capture="environment" do on a mobile file input?
interviewQA.answer: It hints mobile browsers to open the rear-facing camera directly when accept="image/*" or "video/*" is set.

lessons.title: Declarative Shadow DOM & Server-Side Rendering
lessons.summary: Declarative Shadow DOM lets servers stream encapsulated Web Component shadow trees directly in HTML via <template shadowrootmode="open"> with zero JavaScript required for first paint.
explanation: Declarative Shadow DOM lets servers stream encapsulated Web Component shadow trees directly in HTML via <template shadowrootmode="open"> with zero JavaScript required for first paint.

Before Declarative Shadow DOM, Web Components suffered a flash of unstyled content (FOUC) because attachShadow() only ran after JS booted. Now the HTML parser attaches the shadow root immediately as bytes arrive.
Use Declarative Shadow DOM when SSR-ing design system components so crawlers and slow devices receive complete styled markup immediately.

codeExample.title: Zero-JS Server-Rendered Shadow DOM
codeExample.code: Rendered immediately during HTML parsing.

keyPoints: <template shadowrootmode="open"> attaches a shadow root during HTML parsing without JS.
Eliminates Flash of Unstyled Custom Elements (FOUCE) in SSR architectures.
Supports <slot> projection identically to imperative attachShadow().

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling this.attachShadow() blindly in a custom element constructor when DSD already attached one
commonMistakes.fix: Check if (!this.shadowRoot) before calling attachShadow() so SSR hydration does not throw.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using deprecated shadowroot="open" attribute instead of shadowrootmode="open"
commonMistakes.fix: The standardized cross-browser attribute is shadowrootmode="open" or "closed".

interviewQA.question: What problem does Declarative Shadow DOM solve for Web Components?
interviewQA.answer: It allows Shadow DOM trees and scoped <style> blocks to be server-rendered and parsed immediately into HTML before JavaScript downloads or executes.

interviewQA.question: What happens if a custom element upgrades when Declarative Shadow DOM already exists?
interviewQA.answer: this.shadowRoot is already populated, so the class can bind events directly without re-creating the shadow tree.

lessons.title: Internationalization (i18n), RTL & Bidirectional Text
lessons.summary: Truly global HTML marks language changes with lang, text direction with dir="rtl" or dir="auto", and isolates embedded opposite-direction strings using <bdi>.
explanation: Truly global HTML marks language changes with lang, text direction with dir="rtl" or dir="auto", and isolates embedded opposite-direction strings using <bdi>.

Without <bdi> (Bidirectional Isolation), inserting an Arabic or Hebrew username inside an English sentence followed by a number can scramble punctuation and digits due to the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm.
Always set lang and dir on <html>, use dir="auto" for unpredictable user-generated fields, and wrap dynamic usernames in <bdi>.

codeExample.title: Safe Bidirectional Markup with lang, dir & <bdi>
codeExample.code: Top scorer: أحمد — 98 points (Excelente)

keyPoints: lang changes pronunciation rules for screen readers and hyphenation/spellcheck in browsers.
dir="rtl" flips reading order and aligns CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start) automatically.
<bdi> isolates user-supplied text so mixed LTR/RTL punctuation never scrambles.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hardcoding physical left/right layout assumptions instead of dir + logical CSS
commonMistakes.fix: Use dir="rtl" on <html> paired with CSS logical properties (inline-start/end) so layouts mirror effortlessly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Injecting user names directly into mixed-direction strings without <bdi>
commonMistakes.fix: Wrap dynamic user strings in <bdi> so RTL characters do not reorder adjacent numbers or punctuation.

interviewQA.question: When should you use the <bdi> element instead of <span>?
interviewQA.answer: Whenever rendering user-generated text of unknown directionality (such as usernames or search terms) inside surrounding text so bidirectional reordering stays isolated.

interviewQA.question: Why is setting lang on inline foreign-language phrases important?
interviewQA.answer: Screen readers switch voice synthesizers and pronunciation rules to match the inline lang attribute, preventing garbled speech.
